description.es-ES: El libro de los Ejercicios de San Ignacio (1522–1548): anotaciones, cuatro semanas, tres modos de orar, misterios de la vida de Cristo y reglas de discreción de espíritus, con la numeración tradicional [1]–[370]. Texto del Autógrafo.
description.en-US: St. Ignatius's book of the Exercises (1522–1548): annotations, four weeks, three methods of prayer, mysteries of the life of Christ and rules for the discernment of spirits. Spanish text of the Autograph, with its traditional numbering [1]–[370]; English translation from the Autograph by Fr. Elder Mullan, S.J. (1914), with his notes on the manuscript.
description.pt-BR: O livro dos Exercícios de Santo Inácio (1522–1548): anotações, quatro semanas, três modos de orar, mistérios da vida de Cristo e regras de discernimento dos espíritos.

es-ES.editor: Autógrafo (Concordancia ignaciana text, via Documenta Catholica Omnia)

sources.edition: Ejercicios espirituales, Autógrafo, with the traditional paragraph numbers [1]-[370] and sixteenth-century orthography; Documenta Catholica Omnia text layer (47 pp.). The index repeated at the end of the PDF is omitted.
sources.description: Spanish text of the Autograph copy corrected by Ignatius. Rubrics, printed in capitals in the PDF, are set as headings in sentence case with accents restored; the body text is unchanged. No editors' notes in this text.
sources.tierEvidence: Ignatius died in 1556 and the Autograph dates from the 1540s; the modern edition's text is the Autograph itself, distributed by Documenta Catholica Omnia without any copyright claim or licence (its copyright page is a generic notice); free in practice.

sources.edition: The Spiritual Exercises of St. Ignatius of Loyola, translated from the Autograph by Father Elder Mullan, S.J., New York: P. J. Kenedy & Sons, 1914. CCEL proofed e-text. Introductory matter, the papal approbations, the contents list and the index are not included.
sources.description: English translation following the Autograph closely. Mullan's footnotes on the manuscript (the saint's handwritten corrections) are kept as footnotes. The paragraph numbers [1]-[370] are not in this e-text, so they appear in the Spanish only; the chapters follow the Spanish.
sources.tierEvidence: Published in New York in 1914 (public domain in the US, published before 1930); Mullan died in 1925. CCEL marks it Public Domain.
